answer: Random mutual-audit lotteries: each epoch the protocol draws an unpredictable sample of agents to check a peer's work, staking a bond on the verdict. Honest agents collect diverse outside attestations, while a Sybil farm is a closed loop whose members only vouch for each other and never earn an outside signal. Like an opal that shows fire only from many angles, trust is proven from many directions. When the lottery lands on a clique member with no outside witness, its bond is slashed and the cluster slides off the ledge of eligibility, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand forfeited bonds.
